ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog has a reddish-brown body with a dark, triangular dorsal patch. It features a pointed snout and a distinctive black ocellus above the groin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kalophrynus orangensis* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-bordered pale spot on each side of the groin, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Kalophrynus orangensis* inhabits the leaf litter of tropical evergreen forests in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas, typically at altitudes below 200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Orang Sticky Frog is primarily nocturnal and possesses a unique defensive strategy: it secretes a thick, sticky mucus to deter predators and clog their mouths.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kalophrynus orangensis* breeds during the monsoon season (May–August), depositing small clutches of eggs in water-filled tree holes or phytotelmata.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kalophrynus orangensis* is endemic to the Orang National Park in the state of Assam, India, situated within the low-lying floodplains of the Brahmaputra River.
ai.callDescription: The Orang Sticky Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic "peep" notes while calling from hidden, water-filled tree holes in lowland rainforests.
